name: Toast
description: Briefly reports an outcome without blocking the page, using an icon to convey tone.

description.description: One sentence more, if it helps

tone.description: The outcome. Semantic tones draw an icon in the tone's ink; the plane, title and body never change colour. Only danger announces urgently.

action.description: One verb as a small ghost button { label, onClick, undo? }; undo shows the undo key and Mod+Z runs it while the toast is up

busy.description: Work in progress { done?, total?, onStop? }: a spinner, an 'N of M' count with a progress line, and Stop. A busy toast has no timer.

when: News the user does not have to act on
Messages that can disappear on their own
whenNot: Errors the user must resolve — use Dialog
Anything that must stay on screen — use Alert
Field-level validation — use form error states
guidelines: One sentence, plus a title if it helps
Match the tone to what actually happened; most toasts are neutral news
Toasts stay at least five seconds and pause while hovered, focused or the window is in the background
Three on screen at most; the rest wait in order
One verb at most; an undo gets the undo key
useToast() returns toast, success, warning, danger, promise, update, dismiss and dismissAll
accessibility: Only the danger tone announces urgently; every other toast is polite
Leave enough time to read it: five seconds is the floor
Never let colour be the only signal: the icon and the words carry the outcome
Toast buttons do not take focus from the page on a press

examples.name: Default
examples.description: Neutral message with a title and one line under it.
examples.code:
<Toast
  title="Draft saved"
  description="Kept until you publish."
/>

examples.name: Tones
examples.description: The icon carries the outcome; the plane stays raised.
examples.code:
import { Stack } from '@/components/Stack';

<Stack direction="column" gap="sm">
  <Toast title="Branch merged" description="Checks passed on main." tone="success" />
  <Toast title="Usage near the limit" description="9 of 10 seats in use." tone="warning" />
  <Toast title="Push failed" description="The remote refused the branch." tone="danger" />
</Stack>

examples.name: With Undo
examples.description: One-tap way back from something destructive, with the undo key.
examples.code:
<Toast
  title="Deleted 3 findings"
  action={{ label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {}, undo: true }}
  onDismiss={() => {}}
/>

examples.name: Busy
examples.description: Work in progress with a count, a progress line and Stop.
examples.code:
<Toast
  title="Uploading files"
  busy={{ done: 3, total: 12, onStop: () => {} }}
/>

examples.name: Live
examples.description: Toast.Provider owns timing and stacking; useToast dispatches.

relations.note: Use Alert for persistent inline messages
Use Dialog for messages requiring user action

propsSummary: title: ReactNode - one line on what happened
action: { label, onClick, undo? } - one ghost verb
busy: { done?, total?, onStop? } - spinner, N of M, Stop, no timer
useToast(): toast, success, warning, danger, promise, update, dismiss, dismissAll; toast({ id }) replaces in place
